series_key: bi-directional trading and hedging of positions in metatrader 5 using the hedgeterminal panel
mechanism: Full read: HedgeTerminal virtualizes MT5 net positions into MT4-like bi-directional positions via order pairing (closing order magic links to initiating order), deal split/merge arithmetics, local ActivePositions.xml contour, and ExcludeOrders.xml. No market regime, volatility, liquidity, or sequence sensing is built—only trade representation and hedging UI/API.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: AUDCAD Forex demo; VTBR* Moscow Exchange futures; account-level order/deal history
why_new_for_mis: After full read this is execution/position-management infrastructure, not an MIS market sensor.
quote: HedgeTerminal is based on the MetaTrader 5 trading environment and the MQL5 programming language. It does not bring new trading information to the terminal, it simply makes the current trading environment seen from a different angle.

series_key: building a candlestick trend constraint model
mechanism: Classify the forming higher-timeframe (D1) candle as bullish or bearish by comparing lower-TF (M1) prior close to the D1 prior close/open: Close_M1[1+shift] >= Close_D1[1+shift] → bull regime (allow buys only); <= → bear regime (allow sells only). Gate EMA7/EMA21 crossover arrows so off-trend lower-TF signals are suppressed.
data_needed: iMA EMA7/EMA21 on chart TF; CopyClose PERIOD_M1 and PERIOD_D1; iBarShift M1/D1 from chart time
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M1 under D1; Boom 500 Index D1 anatomy on M5; synthetic Boom 500
why_new_for_mis: Treats the live higher-TF candlestick polarity (not an MA) as the primary regime fence for lower-TF signal admission—simple multi-scale polarity sensor for MIS.
quote: This model aims to confine the signal generator to producing signals aligned with the current candle trend.

series_key: building a candlestick trend constraint model
mechanism: Add a slow SMA(400) as trend enforcement vs SMMA(7) as price proxy: buy only when SMMA7 > SMA400 and D1 polarity bullish; sell only when SMMA7 < SMA400 and D1 bearish. Filters residual off-trend arrows that survived the D1 gate alone.
data_needed: iMA SMMA period 7; iMA SMA period 400; D1 open/close via barshift; chart OHLC
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Boom 500 Index; EURUSD M1; PLOT_MAXIMUM_BARS_BACK up to 10000
why_new_for_mis: Stacks a very-slow SMA regime check on top of HTF candle polarity—dual-horizon trend fence usable as MIS regime confirmation.
quote: The restriction dictates buying solely when the price is higher than SMA 400 and selling exclusively when it is lower.

series_key: building a candlestick trend constraint model
mechanism: Replace MA-crossover entries with RSI(14) threshold crosses: buy when RSI crosses below Oversold (default 30) while D1 polarity bullish and SMMA7>SMA400; sell when RSI crosses above Overbought (70) while D1 bearish and SMMA7<SMA400.
data_needed: iRSI(14); Oversold/Overbought inputs; D1 close and M1 open via barshift; SMMA7/SMA400
why_new_for_mis: Momentum exhaustion cross used as entry sensor only inside an HTF+slow-MA regime—MIS can reuse the gated RSI-cross state.
quote: we are removing the MA crossover and instead using RSI levels for entry, along with other recently incorporated conditions

series_key: building a candlestick trend constraint model
mechanism: Add dedicated reversal buffers: EMA(100) cross above SMA(200) → Buy Reversal alert; EMA(100) cross below SMA(200) → Sell Reversal. Separate from D1-constrained continuation signals so the system senses when lower-TF trend invalidates even if D1 day started bearish/bullish.
data_needed: iMA EMA 100; iMA SMA 200; crossover of consecutive bars; audible/push alerts
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPYmicro M5; Boom 300 Index M5; Trend Constraint V1.03 on USDJPY M1
why_new_for_mis: Explicit regime-change channel (MA cross) alongside a static D1 polarity regime—MIS needs both state and transition sensors.
quote: When the two averages cross over, it often signals a change in direction. Having our system detect this and alert us would be very beneficial.

series_key: building ai-powered trading systems in mql5
mechanism: Dispatch-driven AI signal console: each action builds a constrained prompt with shared bar preamble (bullish=close>open; bars newest-first) + Ai_FormatBarsDesc OHLC block; AI must reply line-based KEY:VALUE; Ai_ParseKVResponse extracts SIGNAL/ENTRY/etc. Seven actions: Twin Bars (2 bars), Quick Scalp (10), Daily Signal (today H1), Trend Read (30 bars + anchors), Key Level (50 bars S/R + bounce/break), chart dump, clear drawings.
data_needed: CopyRates OHLC; OpenAI WebRequest; AutoTrade/LotSize; parse keys SIGNAL, level type, bias
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Chart _Symbol/_Period; Daily Signal uses H1 bars; bar counts 2/10/30/50 by action
why_new_for_mis: Turns an LLM into a structured, parseable sequence sensor over fixed bar windows with an explicit bullish/bearish ontology—MIS can ingest KEY:VALUE neural reads instead of free prose.
quote: Each AI-driven action follows a line-based key-value output protocol — one fact per line, no JSON, no nested braces — paired with an explicit bar-direction preamble

instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any symbol via chart; market orders for Twin Bars/Quick Scalp/Daily Signal; pending for Key Level

quote: Stop and target distances use a buffer computed as a fraction of recent bar range, so the same code works on any symbol without per-instrument tuning.

series_key: building a custom market regime detection system in mql5
mechanism: CStatistics.Autocorrelation(lag): corr(series_t, series_{t+lag}). TrendStrength = AC(1); MeanReversionStrength = −AC(1). Positive lag-1 autocorrelation → trending regime tendency; negative → ranging/mean-reverting.
data_needed: Price or returns window; lag parameter (1); mean of series
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic chart symbol/period; lookback default 100; indicator on chart window
why_new_for_mis: Objective statistical trend-vs-range sensor from return autocorrelation—core MIS regime feature distinct from MA/ADX heuristics.
quote: Positive autocorrelation indicates trending behavior, while negative autocorrelation suggests mean-reverting (ranging) behavior.

series_key: building a custom market regime detection system in mql5
mechanism: DetermineRegime hierarchy: (1) if latest rolling vol > avgVol(past ~20 bars)*VolatilityThreshold → REGIME_VOLATILE; (2) else if |TrendStrength| > TrendThreshold → TRENDING_UP/DOWN by priceChange over SmoothingPeriod; (3) else REGIME_RANGING. Enum: TRENDING_UP/DOWN, RANGING, VOLATILE, UNDEFINED.
data_needed: Returns %; rolling stdev window ~20; trend AC window ~50; lookback≥100; TrendThreshold~0.2; VolatilityThreshold~1.5
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any Symbol/PERIOD_CURRENT; MarketRegimeIndicator buffers for regime, trend strength, volatility
why_new_for_mis: Volatility-precedence regime taxonomy (vol beats trend) gives MIS a clean four-state market label with tunable thresholds.
quote: This hierarchical approach ensures that volatility takes precedence over trend detection, as trend-following strategies are particularly vulnerable in volatile markets.

series_key: building a custom market regime detection system in mql5
mechanism: CalculateVolatility: for each bar, stdev of percentage returns over rolling window (min(20, lookback-1)); compare latest to recent average to detect elevated vol. Exposed as VolatilityBuffer and GetVolatility() for chart and EA.
data_needed: Close→% returns; rolling window size; m_volatility array
why_new_for_mis: Explicit rolling return-stdev series as a first-class MIS volatility sensor feeding regime classification.
quote: CalculateVolatility() uses a rolling window approach to calculate the standard deviation of returns at each point in time, providing a measure of market volatility.

series_key: building a custom market regime detection system in mql5
mechanism: MarketRegimeEA: on new bar ProcessData → GetCurrentRegime; TRENDING_UP/DOWN → trend-follow buy/sell with TrendingLot/SL/TP; RANGING → RSI(14) mean-reversion with smaller lots; VOLATILE → Bollinger breakout with smallest lots and wider stops. Comment shows regime, trend strength, volatility.
data_needed: CMarketRegimeDetector; CopyClose lookback; iRSI; iBands; regime-specific lot/SL/TP inputs
why_new_for_mis: Shows MIS regime labels driving mutually exclusive strategy+risk policies—template for regime-conditioned sensing consumers.
quote:
In trending markets, it will use trend-following strategies
- In ranging markets, it will use mean-reversion strategies
- In volatile markets, it will use breakout strategies with reduced position sizes

quote: This function maintains a history of recent regime classifications and returns the most common regime, reducing the impact of temporary fluctuations.
